answer: Each identity posts a 75-credit bond for one grain lot. A kernel sample is weighed wet, dried on copper trays in a quartz dryer, then weighed dry, with weights, tray serials, and quartz readings on a public board. Auditors recompute moisture loss as wet minus dry over wet; outside a 2% tolerance, a reused tray serial, or a copied reading burns the bond. The first lot costs 32 credits, the k-th 32+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6026 and 1000 fakes pay 3,029,000 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-tray ring fails: one tray cannot dry two lots. An honest grower pays 32 once for one kernel lot.
